reading: Grey(5) pieces at the bottom are lifted into the matching holes of the red(2) top band so each piece exactly fills a hole; placed pieces become blue(1) and the bottom is cleared.

slots.pieces: the 5-coloured objects in the lower half
slots.holes: background gaps in the red band whose shape matches a piece
slots.placement: piece shifted (no rotation) so it fills its hole exactly
slots.colour: placed pieces recoloured 1; original piece cells cleared

why: every hole in the red band is filled by exactly one piece of the same shape; the red band is unchanged

reading: The output is the red(2) square outline cut out, with the small 3x3 coloured shape scaled up by an integer factor to fill the outline's interior exactly.

slots.frame: the red rectangular outline (output = its box)
slots.shape: the other object, read in its 3x3 box
slots.paste: scaled shape fills the frame interior

why: output size = outline box; interior = shape upscaled by interior/3

reading: Every hollow 3x3 square of 1s is replaced by a red(2) plus sign in the same 3x3 box (plus centred on the hole, corners cleared); all other shapes stay.

new_rows.name: ring_centre
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inside(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
nonring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !inside(Y2, X2).
nonring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C2), !fgc(Y2, X2).
ring_centre(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), !nonring(Y, X).

why: each background cell fully surrounded by fg (a ring hole) becomes the centre of a 3x3 unit '.2./222/.2.' written over the ring
invariants: objects that are not hollow squares

reading: Objects of 4 or more cells fall straight down until they touch the bottom border; objects of 3 or fewer cells stay where they are.

new_rows.name: big
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N > 3.

why: each object with size >= 4 keeps its shape and its bottom row ends on the last grid row; smaller objects are unchanged

reading: Each 3x3 window that is entirely background(0) is filled with blue(1); where two such windows overlap only the first in reading order is filled.

new_rows.name: empty3
new_rows.datalog:
zero(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0.
inside(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
bad(Y, X) :- inside(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !zero(Y2, X2).
ctr(Y, X) :- zero(Y, X), !bad(Y, X).
blocked(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y2, X2), Y2 < Y, D = Y - Y2, D <= 2, E = X - X2, E <= 2, E >= -2.
blocked(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y, X2), X2 < X, E = X - X2, E <= 2.
keep(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), !blocked(Y, X).
empty3(Y, X) :- keep(Y, X).
empty3(Y, X) :- keep(Y0, X0), off(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX.

why: exactly the 9 cells of each non-overlapping all-0 3x3 window become 1; nothing else changes
invariants: zero cells outside an empty 3x3 window

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels cut by grey(5) lines; the panel containing a yellow(4) cell is copied into the panel whose position matches the 4's position inside its own panel, and every other panel is cleared.

slots.panels: 3x3 grid of 3x3 panels cut by full grey separator lines
slots.source: the one panel that contains colour 4
slots.target: panel at index (row, col) = the 4's local (row, col) inside the source panel
slots.rest: all other panel contents cleared; separators kept

why: output = separators + source panel content pasted at target panel, everything else 0

reading: Under the umbrella-shaped object, each column that has a scattered dot below the umbrella gets a full vertical line in the dot colour from just under the umbrella down to the bottom edge.

new_rows.name: sheltered
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dot(O) :- osize(O, N), N = 1.
umb(O) :- osize(O, N), N > 1.
sheltered(Y, X) :- dot(M), obj(M, Y, X), umb(U), obj(U, Y2, X), Y2 < Y.

why: each sheltered dot extends vertically: upward until the first umbrella cell (not crossing it) and downward to the grid border

reading: Output 3x3 of grey(5) on background chosen by how many colours the input has: 1 colour gives the top row, 2 colours the main diagonal, 3 colours the anti-diagonal.

slots.count: number of distinct colours in the input (1, 2 or 3)
slots.pattern: 1 -> top row filled; 2 -> diagonal TL-BR; 3 -> diagonal TR-BL

why: the output pattern is a fixed function of the input's colour count

reading: Each L-shaped 3-cell object (a 2x2 box missing one corner) shoots a diagonal ray of its own colour from its missing corner outward (away from the object) to the grid edge; the missing corner itself stays empty.
why: every ray starts one diagonal step beyond the missing corner, points away from the L's elbow, and runs until the border

reading: The output is the input placed beside its left-right mirror image with colours inverted (0 -> 8, 2 -> 0); the inverted mirror goes on the side where the shape touches the grid edge (right if it touches the right edge, else left).

slots.copy: horizontal flip of the input with background -> 8 and 2 -> background
slots.side: right of the input if the 2s touch the right edge, otherwise left

why: output halves: one is the input, the other is the flipped, colour-complemented input
